# A basis balance written on the wrong line of the two.
#
# 100.00 USD is bought for 135.00 CAD, and the balance meant for the USD split
# is stated on the CAD one. It passes every test that reads the figure alone —
# 60.00 is a number, is not negative, fits the cent, and is less than the
# 135.00 that line carries — while saying nothing at all: a CAD split in a CAD
# book holds no foreign currency, so no cost basis lives on it and nothing
# will ever read the balance.
#
# Meanwhile the USD split, which is the basis, was never given one, so it
# opens at its full 100.00. The file asked for 60.00 available and the book
# holds 100.00, with no error — the same 40 USD back from the dead that a
# mistyped balance used to produce, reached by putting the line one row up.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_stated_balance_is_checked.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-01-10 * "Buy 100 USD at 1.35"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank:USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.35"
		value: "135.00"
	Assets:Bank -135.00 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "1"
		value: "-135.00"
		cost_basis_available: "60.00"
